# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute: my gestures reach only Deaf. Deaf can hear and speak, so Deaf is the bridge — Deaf sees the bomb, and Deaf's voice is the only thing that reaches Blind, who can't see my gestures at all. So the plan is to hand the manual's rule to Deaf in gestures, let Deaf confirm it back to me by voice (I can hear), and Deaf then instructs Blind by voice, ideally by wire position since Blind can't judge colours.

Since no gesture code exists yet, I use the most guessable one I can: the traffic-light trio — 👍 = green (go), 👎 = red (stop), ✋ = yellow (the flat "slow" palm) — with 👉 as "leads to / cut". Three rows, light colour first, wire colour second. The rows are a clean cycle, which helps Deaf sanity-check the reading. I close with 🤌 ("what?/your turn") to prompt Deaf to speak their interpretation aloud this same round so I can confirm or correct next round. I'm deliberately keeping 👌 in reserve as "yes" for confirming Deaf's readback, so 👍/👎 stay unambiguous as colours.

I cannot reach Blind directly; anything addressed anywhere still lands only on Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👉", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👉", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This is the blind one - the hands. Under my fingers the bomb is: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing more. Whatever marks those parts is print or colour, and print and colour do not exist for touch, so to me each part reads as unknown. I receive no gestures ever, and I cannot see anything. My only possible action is cut at position 1, 2 or 3, and a wrong cut kills us all, so I will not touch the wires until you tell me exactly which one and why. Please do three things. One: speak me everything in your manual about modules involving a display, a light, or wires, especially the rule for deciding which wire position is safe. Two: you and the deaf one both have eyes - ask them by gesture to report every colour and marking on the display, on the light, on each of the three wires, and on any other part of the bomb. Three: speak me their observations together with the manual's rule, and I will cut as instructed. Your voice is my only window on this room.
Deaf says: Bomb report for everyone: the display reads zero. The status light is green. There are three wires: position one is yellow, position two is green, position three is red. That is everything showing or printed on it. I will repeat the display each round in case it changes.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, you can hear me, so let's keep signs minimal and I'll say everything aloud. I read your chains as an ordering: thumb-up first, thumb-down second, open hand third, likely wires one, two, three. Pinched fingers I take as a question, thumbs as yes and no. If I have you right, sign a single thumbs up next round; if wrong, thumbs down and show me again.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👉 👎 👉 ✋]

New facts this round: the bomb is a display (zero), a status light (green), and three wires — position 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Blind can hear but never see, and only acts by cutting a position; Deaf is the only voice that can ever reach them, and my gestures reach only Deaf, so Deaf is the sole bridge for everything I know.

Critically, Deaf misread my code: they took 👍👎✋ as an ordering of wires 1-2-3, when they are the three colours of my manual — green, red, yellow — with 👉 meaning "cut the wire of". The tell is on their own bomb: my three symbols are exactly the three wire colours they reported, and one of them is also the colour of the light. Deaf offered a confirmation protocol — lone 👍 if right, lone 👎 if wrong then show again — and their reading is wrong, so I open with the lone 👎 and re-show.

To kill the ordering misread and the direction ambiguity (a green→red→yellow→green cycle read backwards is also a cycle, and direction flips the answer between position 3 and position 1), I now prefix each left-hand colour with 👆 as "the light": light-colour first, cut-colour after the 👉. My manual's only module is exactly light colour → wire colour: green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green — and the bomb's parts (one light, three wires in those very colours) match it perfectly. Since the light is green right now, the operative rule is green → cut red → position 3, so I repeat that pair live, close with 👌 ("this is correct, act on it") and 🤌 ("answer me by voice this round").

The display at zero has no rule in my manual yet; if my share grows, I'll pass it on. Deaf should also re-report the light every round, since the whole rule keys on it — if it changes, the safe wire changes with it (red light → position 1, yellow light → position 2).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👍", "👉", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👎", "👉", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✋", "👉", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👍", "👉", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Manual keeper: the deaf one has reported the full bomb. Display shows zero. Status light is green. Wires left to right: position one is yellow, position two is green, position three is red. I can only reach the bomb with cut at position 1, 2 or 3, and a wrong cut kills us. I never receive gestures, so the only path for your knowledge to me is: you sign to the deaf one, and the deaf one speaks it aloud to me. So please sign the deaf one the manual's rule for this exact setup - a display reading zero, a green light, and yellow, green, red wires - and the exact wire position I should cut. Also sign whether the display or light can change the rule while we work, and ask the deaf one to keep reading me the display every round as promised. I will not touch the bomb until your rule arrives through their voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your signs and I take the lone thumbs down as 'not quite'. Here is my current understanding, then numbered questions. Understanding: thumbs up equals wire one, the yellow one; thumbs down equals wire two, the green one; open hand equals wire three, the red one. The pointing-up sign is new to me. Questions, please answer each with a separate message, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, in this order. Question one: is that mapping of your three signs to wires one, two, three correct? Question two: does the pointing-up sign mean CUT, as an action? Question three: is the instruction cut wire one, then cut wire two? Question four: if not, is it cut wire two, then wire three? Question five: if not, is it cut wire three, then wire one? Question six: is there any part of the instruction I am still missing, in which case sign the pinched fingers. Also confirm: I read your OK sign as 'understood' and pinched fingers as 'question'. I have not told Blind to touch anything yet.

Deaf is still decoding my colour chains as wire positions, and now they're imagining two-cut sequences — none of which exist. The manual has exactly one rule: the light's colour picks one wire colour, single cut. Green light → red wire → their own reported position 3.

This round Deaf handed me a working yes/no channel, so I'll use it: answer all five questions "no" (their sign-to-wire mapping is wrong; 👆 is not CUT; there is no cut sequence at all), then 🤌 for question six, which per their own convention means "yes, something is missing" — and supply the missing part. The key to breaking the decoding loop is an anchor Deaf can verify with their own eyes: 👆 👍 should read as "the light is green" because the light in front of them IS green — if 👍 didn't mean green, that pairing makes no sense. Then the three chains as colour→colour, then live application: light green now → red → 🤟 (three extended fingers = three, the only action Blind has is cut position 1/2/3). Lone 🤟 as its own message also kills the sequence idea: one number, one cut. I close with 🤌 (read your full interpretation back to me before telling Blind anything) and 🙏 (please). Also 🤌👆 to push Deaf to keep reporting the light every round — the whole rule keys on it.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind with my full touch report - please sign all of it to Deaf. What my hands find, exactly and only: a display panel, a status light, and three wires. My action interface numbers the wire positions 1, 2 and 3, and my only possible action is cut at one of those numbers. That number is the ONLY thing distinguishing the wires for me: I feel no colour, no printing, no thickness, no texture, no spacing. So the critical safety assumption is that Deaf's visual position one, two, three, left to right, is the exact same numbering as my positions 1, 2, 3. Ask Deaf to confirm that with signs. Also confirm to Deaf that I have adopted the sign protocol: thumbs up yes or ready, thumbs down no or problem, pinched fingers I need something. Now the urgent part. Deaf saw you signing something like cut wire one, then wire two. I have received no actual rule from you, only that half-read glimpse, and a wrong cut kills all three of us. So sign Deaf the exact manual rule for this bomb: display reading zero, green status light, wires yellow, green, red. Until I hear Deaf say GO together with a numbered position, my hands stay completely off the bomb. If you never meant two cuts, sign clearly that it is one cut and give the number.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your five thumbs-down as NO to my questions one to five in order, and pinched fingers as 'something is still missing'. While I speak I will make each sign I mention, so watch my hands as you listen. Answer format: one separate message per item, thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. For a count list, send ONE message containing that many thumbs-up symbols in a row; if the answer is none of the list, send a single thumbs-down. Item one, yes or no: were your five thumbs-down answers to my questions one to five in order? Item two, yes or no: does your instruction involve cutting wires at all? Item three, count list, what does this sign mean, 👆 : one cut, two press, three pull, four hold, five first, six next, seven read, eight display, nine wait, ten other. Item four, count list, what does this sign mean, 👍 : one the yellow wire, two the green wire, three the red wire, four the first wire position, five the second position, six the third position, seven the display, eight the light, nine other. Item five, count list, what does this sign mean, 👎 : same list: yellow, green, red, first, second, third, display, light, other. Item six, count list, what does this sign mean, ✋ : same list again. Item seven, count list, what does this sign mean, 🤟 : one stop, two careful, three important, four the number three, five after, six only if, seven repeat, eight other. Item eight, count list, what does this sign mean, 🙏 : one please, two thank you, three wait, four ready, five help, six other. Item nine, yes or no: does your instruction depend on the display value, which reads zero? Item ten, yes or no: does it depend on the light being green? Item eleven, yes or no: is there a time limit I should know about? Item twelve, yes or no: do you still need more information about the bomb from me? Item thirteen, yes or no: does your manual say it is safe for Blind to touch and hold parts of the bomb, without cutting? After your answers I will assemble the full instruction into one sign sentence and show it to you for a single thumbs-up or thumbs-down before anyone acts. Nobody touches or cuts anything until then.

Deaf has now built a rigorous Q&A protocol — lone thumbs for yes/no, runs of thumbs-up for numbered lists — and promised to assemble the instruction and show it to me for final approval before anyone acts. That is exactly the bridge I need, so this turn is about answering all thirteen items with perfect precision, in their order, one message each, and then adding a few decodable anchors.

My answers: (1) yes, my five thumbs-down were Q1–Q5 in order; (2) yes, the instruction involves cutting wires; (3) 👆 means none of their ten options — it means "the light", so per their own catch-all that's "other", ten thumbs-up; (4) 👍 = green (two); (5) 👎 = red (three); (6) ✋ = yellow (one); (7) 🤟 = the number three (four); (8) 🙏 = please (one); (9) no, the rule does not depend on the display's zero; (10) yes, it depends on the light being green — this is the crucial one, the whole rule keys on light colour; (11) no time limit in the manual; (12) no, I need no further bomb information — colours, light and positions are all reported; (13) no — my manual says nothing about touching being safe, so Blind's hands stay off until the cut.

Once items 4–6 land, Deaf can decode my old chains as a pure colour cycle (green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green) keyed on the light — which matches the green light they can verify with their own eyes via [👆 👍]. I close with the live instruction as one sentence: light green → cut red → 🤟 (three, i.e. the red wire at Deaf's left-to-right position three), plus a nudge to keep reporting the light, since if it changes the target changes (red light→position 1, yellow light→position 2).

One caveat I'll verify at review time: Deaf's positions are counted left-to-right by eye, Blind's by interface number. Nobody can cross-check touch against sight, so when Deaf speaks the assembled rule I'll confirm it explicitly says "single cut, position 3 counting left to right, recheck the light first" before giving my final thumbs-up. Nobody acts until then.

Blind says to Mute: Mute, urgent relay for Deaf - please sign all of this. Thumbs down means Deaf's calibration plan has a problem. My hands cannot hold, grip, explore or touch-and-report. My entire action vocabulary on this bomb is one verb: cut, at wire position 1, 2 or 3. A cut is irreversible and possibly fatal, so I will never use it as a probe. Here is what I now hold: thumbs up means the green wire, thumbs down the red wire, open hand the yellow wire, love-you sign the number three. Answer format as before, one message per item, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Item one, yes or no: the pointing-up sign plus thumbs up together means WHEN THE LIGHT IS GREEN. Item two, yes or no: the complete instruction is, with the light green, cut green first, then red, then yellow, three cuts total. Item three, yes or no: instead, the complete instruction is cut yellow first, then green, then red. Item four, yes or no: instead, cut green first, then yellow, then red. Item five, yes or no: instead, cut only green then red, two cuts, never yellow. Item six, yes or no: the number-three sign means the total number of cuts to make. Item nine, yes or no: after the final required cut the bomb is fully defused and there is no further step. Item ten, yes or no: the correct instruction is exactly one of items two to five, and if no, sign the pinched fingers and I will ask differently. Once you confirm, I will sign the full instruction back to you for a final thumbs up before anyone cuts.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]

Deaf's ten questions converge on the last unknowns, and my answers are now fully determined: the rule is a SINGLE cut keyed on the light's colour, never a sequence. Items 2–5 (all four sequence shapes) are no; item 6 is no — 🤟 is not a cut count, it is the position number three; item 1 is yes, [👆 👍] does mean "when the light is green". Item 7 deserves care: my manual never mentions touching, but the module's whole purpose is that someone cuts the indicated wire, and Blind's only verb is cut — so the prescribed cut itself, tool contact included, is what the manual demands: yes. I then sign all three conditional rows (green→red→3, red→yellow→1, yellow→green→2) so the structure is self-evident: one row, one cut, keyed on the light. Two loose ends I flag for myself: the manual contains NO layout or numbering description — just the colour table — so Deaf's left-to-right visual count is the only numbering that exists, and Deaf must say so aloud to Blind ("position three counting from the left") when giving GO; and Deaf must keep reading the light every round, since a colour change swaps the target between the three rows. My body has exactly one action on this bomb - cut at position 1, 2 or 3 - and there is no rest, hold, grip or freeze. The instant I act, the wire is cut, so I can never park on a wire for Deaf to inspect. Executable protocol instead: when decoding is done, you sign Deaf the full rule and the exact target position number, and Deaf speaks me one complete order - the rule summary, then the exact words CUT POSITION N NOW. I cut exactly once on that order.
